extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, agents, and applicants filing international design applications and recording documents with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and documentary requirements for filing, prosecuting, converting, and recording international design applications that designate the United States, and for recording assignments and related documents with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in an international design application (§ 1.1041)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may appoint a representative before the International Bureau in accordance with Rule 3. Applicants of international design applications may be represented before the Office as an office of indirect filing by a practitioner registered (§ 11.6) or granted limited recognition (§ 11.9(a) or (b)) to practice before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment must be in writing signed by the applicant, must give the practitioner power to act on behalf of the applicant, and must specify the name and registration number or limited recognition number of each practitioner. A practitioner may act pursuant to § 1.34 or pursuant to appointment by the applicant. An appointment made in the international design application pursuant to Rule 3(2) that complies with these requirements will be effective as an appointment before the Office as an office of indirect filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address for international design applications (§ 1.1042)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may specify a correspondence address for correspondence sent by the Office as an office of indirect filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no such address has been specified, the Office will use as the correspondence address the address of applicant’s appointed representative (§ 1.1041) or, where no representative is appointed, the address as specified in Administrative Instruction 302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of international design application to the International Bureau (§ 1.1045)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (b) and payment of the transmittal fee, transmittal of the international design application to the International Bureau shall be made by the Office as provided by Rule 13(1). At the same time the Office transmits the application it shall notify the International Bureau of the date it received the application and shall notify the applicant of the date received and of the transmittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No copy may be transmitted to the International Bureau, a foreign designated office, or other foreign authority by the Office or the applicant unless the applicable requirements of part 5 have been satisfied. Once transmittal has been effected, except for matters properly before the USPTO as an office of indirect filing or as a designated office, all further correspondence concerning the application should be sent directly to the International Bureau. The USPTO will generally not forward communications received after transmittal. Any reply to an invitation sent to the applicant by the International Bureau must be filed directly with the International Bureau, and not with the Office, to avoid abandonment or other loss of rights under Article 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief from prescribed time limits; petition requirements (§ 1.1051)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the delay in failing to act within prescribed time limits under the Hague Agreement was unintentional, a petition may be filed to excuse the failure to act as to the United States. A grantable petition must be accompanied by specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition must include: (1) a copy of any invitation sent from the International Bureau setting the prescribed time limit at issue; (2) the reply required under paragraph (c) unless previously filed; (3) the fee set forth in § 1.17(m); (4) a certified copy of the originally filed international design application, unless previously communicated to the Office, and a translation into English if filed in another language; (5) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional (the Director may require additional information); and (6) a terminal disclaimer and fee as required by paragraph (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for reconsideration of petition refusals (§ 1.1051(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to excuse failure to act must be filed within two months of the decision or within such time set in the decision. Unless indicated otherwise, this period may be extended under § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness rules and § 1.136 extension provisions apply to reconsideration requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible replies when seeking relief (§ 1.1051(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply required in connection with a petition under § 1.1051 may be either the filing of a continuing application or a grantable petition under § 1.1052 where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing a continuing application and the international design application has not been subject to international registration, the reply must include a grantable petition under § 1.1023(b) to accord a filing date. Where the international design application was filed with the Office as an office of indirect filing, the reply may be a grantable petition under § 1.1052.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer with petitions for relief (§ 1.1051(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition under this section must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer and fee dedicating to the public a terminal part of the term of any patent granted thereon equal to the period of delay from the due date of the reply until the filing of the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must also apply to any patent granted on a continuing design application that contains a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c) or 386(c) to the application for which relief is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of international design application to U.S. design application (§ 1.1052)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States filed with the Office as an office of indirect filing and meeting § 1.53(b) filing-date requirements may, on petition, be converted to an application for a design patent under § 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(t) and filed prior to publication of the international registration under Article 10(3). Conversion will not entitle applicant to refund of transmittal fee or other forwarded fees. The resulting application must include basic filing fee (§ 1.16(b)), search fee (§ 1.16(l)), examination fee (§ 1.16(p)), the inventor’s oath or declaration (§ 1.63 or 1.64), and any applicable surcharge (§ 1.16(f)). A conversion decision is effective to convert only if granted prior to transmittal to the International Bureau; otherwise it is effective only for purposes of U.S. designation. A petition will not be granted in an abandoned international design application absent a grantable petition under § 1.1051.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of general patent rules to international design applications (§ 1.1061)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules relating to applications for patents for other inventions or discoveries are also applicable to international design applications designating the United States, except as otherwise provided in this chapter or required by the Articles or Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific provisions excluded from applicability include § 1.74, § 1.84 except for § 1.84(c), and §§ 1.152 through 1.154.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination timing for international design applications (§ 1.1062)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make an examination pursuant to title 35 of an international design application designating the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Rule 18(1)(c)(ii), the Office shall send to the International Bureau within 12 months from publication of the international registration under Rule 26(3) a notification of refusal (§ 1.1063) where it appears the applicant is not entitled to a patent for any industrial design that is the subject of the international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in a Notification of Refusal (§ 1.1063)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification of refusal shall contain or indicate: (1) the number of the international registration; (2) the grounds on which the refusal is based; (3) a copy of a reproduction of the earlier industrial design and information concerning it when grounds refer to similarity; (4) identify which designs are affected when refusal does not relate to all designs; and (5) a time period for reply under §§ 1.134 and 1.136 where reply is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reply to the notification of refusal must be filed directly with the Office (not through the International Bureau). The requirements of § 1.111 apply to replies to a notification of refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: One independent and distinct design per nonprovisional international design application (§ 1.1064)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one independent and distinct design may be claimed in a nonprovisional international design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements are not satisfied, the examiner shall in the notification of refusal or other Office action require the applicant to elect one independent and distinct design for which prosecution on the merits shall be restricted. Such requirement will normally be made before any action on the merits but may be made any time before final action. Review of such requirement is provided under §§ 1.143 and 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, description, and inventor’s oath or declaration for international design applications (§ 1.1067)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must designate the particular article. No description other than a reference to the drawing is ordinarily required. An international design application designating the United States must include the inventor’s oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no title is contained, the Office may establish a title. If applicant is notified in a notice of allowability that an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63 or substitute statement in compliance with § 1.64 has not been filed, the applicant must file each required oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63 or § 1.64 no later than the date on which the issue fee is paid to avoid abandonment. This time period is not extendable under § 1.136 (see § 1.136(c)). See § 1.1021(d) re oath/declaration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grant of protection (§ 1.1068)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of a patent on an international design application designating the United States, the Office may send to the International Bureau a statement to the effect that protection is granted in the United States to those industrial design or designs that are the subject of the international registration and covered by the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of invalidation (§ 1.1070)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a design patent granted from an international design application is invalidated in the United States and the invalidation is no longer subject to review or appeal, the patentee shall inform the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving notification of invalidation or through other means, the Office will notify the International Bureau in accordance with Hague Rule 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of protection only upon patent issuance (§ 1.1071)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant of protection for an industrial design that is the subject of an international registration shall only arise in the United States through the issuance of a patent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 389(d) or 171, and in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 153.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to recording and assignments (Part 3, § 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for Application, Assignment, Document, Office, Recorded document, and Registration used in Part 3: 'Application' includes national applications, international patent applications designating the U.S., international design applications designating the U.S., and trademark applications under specified statutes; 'Assignment' means transfer of all or part of right, title and interest; 'Document' means a document requested to be recorded affecting interest in application, patent, or registration; 'Office' means the USPTO; 'Recorded document' means document recorded pursuant to § 3.11; 'Registration' means a trademark registration issued by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions govern the interpretation and application of Part 3 recording rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents eligible for recording (§ 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of applications, patents, and registrations, and other documents relating to interests in patent applications and patents, accompanied by completed cover sheets as specified in § 3.28 and § 3.31, will be recorded. Other documents affecting title, accompanied by completed cover sheets, will be recorded as provided or at Director's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Order 9424 requires government departments and agencies to forward licenses, assignments, or interests of the Government in patents or patent applications for recording. A joint research agreement or an excerpt thereof will also be recorded as provided in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignability of trademarks prior to filing an allegation of use (§ 3.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an allegation of use (15 U.S.C. 1051(c) or 1051(d)) is filed, an applicant may only assign an application to register a mark under 15 U.S.C. 1051(b) to a successor to the applicant’s business, or portion of the business to which the mark pertains, if that business is ongoing and existing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required in assignments (§ 3.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment relating to a patent must identify the patent by patent number. An assignment relating to a national patent application must identify the national patent application by application number (series code and serial number). An assignment relating to an international patent application designating the U.S. must identify the international application by number (e.g., PCT/US2012/012345). An assignment relating to an international design application must identify the international design application by international registration number or by the U.S. application number assigned to the international design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignment of a patent application filed under § 1.53(b) is executed concurrently with or subsequent to execution of the patent application but before filing, it must identify the patent application by each inventor name and the title of the invention to avoid mistake. Similar rule applies to provisional applications under § 1.53(c) executed before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for documents and cover sheets (format and submission) (§ 3.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic submissions: either a copy or an extract of the original document may be submitted; all documents must be submitted as digitized images in TIFF or another form prescribed by the Director. When printed to standard paper sizes the document must be legible and a 2.5 cm (one-inch) margin present on all sides. For paper or facsimile submissions: copy or extract must be submitted, one side only, standardized paper sizes, one-inch margins, paper should be flexible, strong white, non-shiny and durable; original documents must not be submitted for recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not return recorded documents; follow image format, size, margin, and paper quality requirements to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording requirements for trademark applications and registrations (§ 3.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: To record documents affecting title to a trademark application or registration, submit a legible cover sheet (see § 3.31) and one of: (1) a copy of the original document; (2) a copy of an extract evidencing the effect on title; or (3) a statement signed by both parties explaining how the conveyance affects title. Name changes require only a legible cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documents for electronic submissions must be digitized images (TIFF or prescribed form) with one-inch margins when printed. Paper submissions must be white, non-shiny, appropriate size, one side only, one-inch margins, originals not to be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language requirement (§ 3.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept and record non-English language documents only if accompanied by an English translation signed by the individual making the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address for submitting documents to be recorded (§ 3.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and cover sheets submitted by mail for recordation should be addressed to Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450, unless filed with new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for recording; single cover sheet requirement (§ 3.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document submitted to the Office for recording must include a single cover sheet (as specified in § 3.31) referring either to those patent applications and patents, or to those trademark applications and registrations, against which the document is to be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a document includes interests in both patents and trademarks, separate patent and trademark cover sheets, each accompanied by a copy of the document, must be submitted. Documents not accompanied by a completed cover sheet will be returned for proper completion; resubmission required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet content requirements (§ 3.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each patent or trademark cover sheet required by § 3.28 must contain: (1) name of the party conveying the interest; (2) name and address of the party receiving the interest; (3) description of the interest conveyed or transaction; (4) identification of the interests involved (application/registration/patent numbers or copies when numbers not known); (5) name and address for correspondence about the recording request; (6) date the document was executed; (7) signature of the party submitting the document (with specified electronic signature formats); and (8) for trademark assignments, entity and citizenship of the receiving party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: If receiving party is domestic partnership/joint venture, cover sheet must list names/legal entities/national citizenship (or state/country of organization) of all general partners/active members. A cover sheet should not refer to both patents and trademarks because information submitted with a trademark request becomes public record. Patent cover sheets seeking to record a governmental interest must indicate that fact and whether the document does not affect title (§ 3.31(c)). Trademark cover sheets should include identification/description of the trademark and citizenship of the conveying party. Joint research agreement submissions must identify the document as such, indicate owner of the application/patent, each other party, and execution date. Certain Patent Law Treaty model forms satisfy assignment cover sheet requirements; an assignment cover sheet used as an oath/declaration under § 1.63 must contain a conspicuous indication of such intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of cover sheet errors (§ 3.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a cover sheet recorded pursuant to § 3.11 will be corrected only if: (1) the error is apparent when the cover sheet is compared with the recorded document to which it pertains; and (2) a corrected cover sheet is filed for recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrected cover sheet must be accompanied by a copy of the document originally submitted for recording and by the recording fee as set forth in § 3.41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fees (§ 3.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests to record documents must be accompanied by the appropriate fee. Except as provided in paragraph (b), a fee is required for each application, patent and registration against which the document is recorded as identified in the cover sheet. Recording fee amounts are set in § 1.21(h) for patents and in § 2.6(b)(6) for trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required for each patent application and patent against which a document required by Executive Order 9424 is to be filed if: (1) the document does not affect title and is so identified in the cover sheet; and (2) the document and cover sheet are faxed or electronically submitted as prescribed by the Director, or mailed in compliance with § 3.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording date rules (§ 3.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording of a document is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording set forth in this part is filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document not complying with identification requirements of § 3.21 will not be recorded. Documents not meeting other requirements (e.g., missing completed cover sheet or required fee) will be returned for correction; returned papers, stamped with original date of receipt, will indicate a period within which corrected resubmission will preserve the original date as the recording date. If returned papers are not corrected and resubmitted within the specified period, the date of filing of the corrected papers will be the date of recording. The specified resubmission period is not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recording (§ 3.54)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recording of a document pursuant to § 3.11 is not a determination by the Office of the validity of the document or the effect that document has on the title to an application, a patent, or a registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, the Office will determine what effect a document has, including whether a party has the authority to take an action in a matter pending before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional assignments treated as absolute for Office purposes (§ 3.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments which are made conditional on the performance of certain acts or events, such as the payment of money or other condition subsequent, if recorded in the Office, are regarded as absolute assignments for Office purposes until cancelled with the written consent of all parties or by the decree of a court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not determine whether such conditions have been fulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governmental registers (§ 3.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading present addressing governmental registers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content not present in this chunk; see full Part 3 text for details on governmental registers and related recording rules.
